jsonLd.name: Dr CM Ngwey-Sompo Inc. — Specialist Obstetrician & Gynaecologist
Antenatal care
jsonLd.description: Antenatal care is the steady, unhurried part of pregnancy — regular visits to check how you and your baby are doing, and time to ask the questions that come up between them.
jsonLd.howPerformed: What antenatal care covers: Each visit reviews your health and your baby's growth, and checks anything that has changed since the last appointment. Blood pressure, weight and the baby's position and heartbeat are the usual measures; what is checked at each stage depends on how far along you are. Planning the birth: Conversations about birth begin well before the third trimester. Preferences, previous experiences and any concerns are discussed openly, alongside what is medically advisable in your case. Care after delivery: The fourth trimester matters as much as the first three. Postnatal review covers your recovery, how feeding is going, and how you are feeling — physically and otherwise.

jsonLd.name: Dr CM Ngwey-Sompo Inc. — Specialist Obstetrician & Gynaecologist
Vaginal & caesarean delivery
jsonLd.description: Delivery care at Life Roseacres Hospital, with the mode of birth decided on clinical need and your preferences — and explained well before the day itself.
jsonLd.howPerformed: Vaginal delivery: Where labour is progressing normally and there is no reason to intervene, vaginal delivery is supported with as little interference as possible. Caesarean delivery: A caesarean may be planned in advance, or become advisable during labour. Either way the reasoning is explained, and consent is taken properly — not assumed. After the birth: You are reviewed in hospital before discharge, and again afterwards. Feeding, wound care where relevant, and your own recovery are all part of that review.

jsonLd.name: Dr CM Ngwey-Sompo Inc. — Specialist Obstetrician & Gynaecologist
General gynaecological consultations
jsonLd.description: A confidential space to discuss symptoms, cycles, contraception or any concern about your reproductive health — at your pace, in language that makes sense.
jsonLd.howPerformed: What a consultation involves: The appointment starts with your history: what brought you in, what you have noticed, and what you are worried about. That conversation usually takes longer than the examination. Common reasons to be seen: Changes in your cycle, pain, bleeding that concerns you, contraception advice, screening, and questions about fertility all belong in a general consultation. Screening and prevention: Cervical screening, HPV vaccination status and breast awareness are reviewed as part of routine care, with the reasoning explained rather than assumed.

jsonLd.name: Dr CM Ngwey-Sompo Inc. — Specialist Obstetrician & Gynaecologist
Female screening & oncology assessment
jsonLd.description: Assessment when a concern needs a closer look — including abnormal screening results — with clear onward referral where specialist oncology input is the right next step.
jsonLd.howPerformed: What this assessment is for: An abnormal cervical screening result, postmenopausal bleeding, a suspicious finding on examination, or a family history that warrants review are all reasons for assessment. Investigation and referral: Where a procedure such as a colposcopy or a biopsy is needed, it is explained beforehand: what it involves, what it feels like, and what the result will tell you. Cervical health and HPV: Dr Sompo's research at Wits examined margin status after LLETZ in women living with HIV, and her special interest in HPV prevention shapes how screening and follow-up are discussed.

jsonLd.howPerformed: How the assessment works: The first appointment covers both partners where possible: your history, your cycles, any previous investigations, and how long you have been trying. What can be done here: Assessment, investigation and interpretation of results happen in this practice. Where treatment requires a specialist fertility unit or laboratory, referral is arranged — and the reason is explained. Emotional and practical weight: Fertility investigations are tiring, and the waiting between results is often harder than the tests. That is treated as part of the clinical picture, not a distraction from it.

mainEntity.name: How do I make an appointment?

acceptedAnswer.text: Appointment enquiries are handled by telephone on 011 842 7651 or by email to chrisscrcross2013@gmail.com. WhatsApp enquiry will be offered once the practice confirms a WhatsApp-enabled number. Submitting an enquiry does not constitute a confirmed appointment — the practice will confirm your date and time directly.

mainEntity.name: What should I bring to my first consultation?

acceptedAnswer.text: Please bring your ID or passport, your medical aid card if you have one, a list of current medications, and any previous results, scans or referral letters that are relevant. If you are pregnant, bring any antenatal records you already have.

mainEntity.name: Where does Dr Sompo consult?

acceptedAnswer.text: Dr Sompo practises at Life Roseacres Hospital, on the corner of St Joseph and Castor Road, Primrose, Germiston, Johannesburg. Please confirm the exact consulting-room and address details with the practice when you book.

mainEntity.name: Does the practice accept medical aid?

acceptedAnswer.text: Please confirm medical aid arrangements, tariffs and any co-payment directly with the practice before your visit. The website does not publish billing details on the practice's behalf.

mainEntity.name: Can I ask clinical questions through the website?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. This website is not a clinical channel. Please do not send symptoms, results or other sensitive medical information through the enquiry form or by email. Clinical questions are best discussed in a consultation, and urgent concerns should be directed to the hospital or your nearest emergency department.

mainEntity.name: In what languages can I be seen?

acceptedAnswer.text: Consultations are available in English and French.

mainEntity.name: Is my enquiry handled confidentially?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Enquiries are received by the practice and handled in line with South African privacy law, including the Protection of Personal Information Act (POPIA). Only the minimum information needed to arrange your appointment is requested.

jsonLd.howPerformed: Choosing the approach: Laparoscopic (keyhole) surgery usually means smaller incisions and a shorter recovery than open surgery. It is not automatically the better option: the right approach depends on what is being treated, previous surgery, and what is safe in your case. What is treated: Ovarian and other gynaecological cysts, fibroids, early-stage endometriosis, and hysterectomy including total laparoscopic hysterectomy are all within the scope described for this practice. Recovery: Recovery time varies by procedure and by person. The expected course is explained before surgery, along with the signs that should prompt you to call rather than wait.
